hook.en: Copper carries current easily and glass not at all. Silicon sits in between, and that in-between nature is what runs every phone and computer.
hook.kn: ತಾಮ್ರ ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಹರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಗಾಜು ಹರಿಸುವುದೇ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಸಿಲಿಕಾನ್ ಇವೆರಡರ ನಡುವೆ; ಅದೇ ಪ್ರತಿ ಫೋನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ ನಡೆಸುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Explain conductors, insulators and semiconductors using energy bands

narration.en: Copper carries current easily and glass not at all. Silicon sits in between, and that in-between nature is what runs every phone and computer.
narration.kn: ತಾಮ್ರ ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಹರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಗಾಜು ಹರಿಸುವುದೇ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಸಿಲಿಕಾನ್ ಇವೆರಡರ ನಡುವೆ; ಅದೇ ಪ್ರತಿ ಫೋನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ ನಡೆಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Metals have very low resistivity ($10^{-2}$ to $10^{-8}$ Ω m), insulators very high ($10^{11}$ to $10^{19}$ Ω m), and semiconductors lie in between ($10^{-5}$ to $10^{6}$ Ω m). Semiconductors can be elemental, such as Si and Ge, or compounds such as GaAs, CdS and organic polymers.
body.kn: ಲೋಹಗಳ ರೋಧಕತೆ ಬಹಳ ಕಡಿಮೆ, ನಿರೋಧಕಗಳದು ಬಹಳ ಹೆಚ್ಚು, ಅರೆವಾಹಕಗಳು ನಡುವೆ. Si, Ge ಧಾತು ಅರೆವಾಹಕಗಳು; GaAs, CdS ಸಂಯುಕ್ತ ಅರೆವಾಹಕಗಳು.

narration.en: Let us draw the energy bands of a metal, an insulator and a semiconductor side by side.

say.en: In a metal, the conduction band overlaps the valence band, so electrons move freely.
In an insulator, a wide gap of more than 3 eV separates the full valence band from the empty conduction band.
In a semiconductor the gap is small, under 3 eV, so heat can lift a few electrons across.
Resistivities show the same three groups.
Diamond has a gap of 5.4 eV; silicon 1.1 eV and germanium 0.7 eV. Silicon absorbs light only if λ is shorter than about 1130 nm.

body.en: In a crystal, the energy levels of atoms spread into bands. The highest filled band is the valence band; above it is the conduction band, separated by the energy gap $E_g$. In metals the bands overlap or the conduction band is partly filled. Insulators have $E_g > 3$ eV, so no electrons can cross at room temperature. Semiconductors have $E_g < 3$ eV (Si 1.1 eV, Ge 0.71 eV), so a few electrons are thermally excited, and more as temperature rises.
body.kn: ಸ್ಫಟಿಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳು ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳಾಗುತ್ತವೆ: ವೇಲೆನ್ಸ್ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮತ್ತು ವಹನ ಪಟ್ಟಿ, ನಡುವೆ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಅಂತರ Eg. ಲೋಹಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳು ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ನಿರೋಧಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ Eg > 3 eV; ಅರೆವಾಹಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ Eg < 3 eV.

points.en: Semiconductor: Eg < 3 eV (Si 1.1 eV, Ge 0.71 eV)

title.en: Try it: band gap and temperature

narration.en: Change the band gap and the temperature; see why silicon conducts a little and diamond almost not at all.

caption.en: How likely is an electron to be thermally lifted across a gap Eg? The graph shows log₁₀ of exp(−Eg/2kT) against temperature.

tryThis.en: Compare Si (1.1 eV) and diamond (5.4 eV) at 300 K. How many powers of ten apart are they?
Heat silicon to 600 K. How much does the log rise?
Why does a semiconductor's resistance fall when it is heated?

problem.en: What is the longest wavelength of light that can lift an electron across the gap in silicon (Eg = 1.1 eV) and in diamond (Eg = 5.4 eV)?

steps.en: Diamond: 1240/5.4 ≈ 230 nm (ultraviolet), so visible light passes through diamond.

points.en: Semiconductors lie between metals and insulators in resistivity.

points.en: Metal: overlapping bands; insulator: Eg > 3 eV; semiconductor: Eg < 3 eV.
points.kn: ಲೋಹ: ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಿಸುವ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳು; ನಿರೋಧಕ: Eg > 3 eV; ಅರೆವಾಹಕ: Eg < 3 eV.

points.en: A semiconductor's resistivity falls as temperature rises.

homework.en: Draw the energy band diagrams of a metal, an insulator and a semiconductor.

narration.en: Recap. Semiconductors lie between metals and insulators in resistivity. Metal: overlapping bands; insulator: Eg > 3 eV; semiconductor: Eg < 3 eV. A semiconductor's resistivity falls as temperature rises.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ರೋಧಕತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅರೆವಾಹಕಗಳು ಲೋಹ ಮತ್ತು ನಿರೋಧಕಗಳ ನಡುವೆ. ಲೋಹ: ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಿಸುವ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳು; ನಿರೋಧಕ: Eg > 3 eV; ಅರೆವಾಹಕ: Eg < 3 eV. ತಾಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದಂತೆ ಅರೆವಾಹಕದ ರೋಧಕತೆ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.
